summary: Hospital floor watch pack. The lead watcher is the IV guardian: it counts the drip rate in the chamber, tracks bag level, watches the insertion site for swelling, and warns the nurse before the bag runs dry. Around it: a turn watcher that verifies real patient turns, a waiting room watcher that re-triages continuously, and a code recorder that keeps the event timeline. Health data rules everything: raw video and vitals never leave the building, and patient identifiers never appear in any bus message. SPEC ONLY: this is a pack definition, not a running hospital system.

urgency.meaning: Code events, suspected infiltration, waiting room deterioration. Preempts everything else on the bus.
Turn windows closing, diversion changes, bags about to run dry.
Sealed code timelines and end-of-shift summaries.

inputs: pole camera feed (stays in the building)
set rate from the pump order
watchers.watches: LEAD WATCHER. The IV pole: drip chamber rate counted from the pole camera, bag level tracked against the set rate, the insertion site watched for swelling that suggests infiltration, and a projected empty time so the nurse gets a pre-alarm (bag empty in about 20 minutes) instead of a pump alarm after the fact.

inputs: bed watch feed (stays in the building)
watchers.watches: Patient turning for pressure injury prevention: whether a real turn happened inside each two hour window, verified from the bed watch, with a reminder before the window closes rather than a missed chart entry after it.

inputs: waiting room camera feed (stays in the building)
watchers.watches: The emergency department waiting room: continuous re-triage of people waiting, flagging anyone whose visible condition worsens (slumping, distress, no response when called) between the triage at the door and being seen.

inputs: scribe entries from the care team
watchers.watches: Code events: the timeline of a resuscitation as it happens, times of drugs given, shocks delivered, and interventions, kept in order as the verified record of the event.
